To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Pol III complex binding leads to altered Pol II transcription of neighboring genes and intergenic DNA in yeast, that these effects occur at the transcriptional start site, and that they influence expression at the translational level.

RNA polymerase III transcription factor mutants exhibit local alterations of RNA polymerase II intergenic transcription that may reflect a role of RNA polymerase III complexes in regulating expression of nearby genes.
RNA sequencing reveals that transcription factor TFII3 depleted mutants have altered intergenic RNA polymeras II transcription in the regions near TFIIIC sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that govern gene expression and how the assembly of the Pol III transcription complex impacts the expression of other genes in yeast.
the role of Pol III transcription in gene expression and chromatin organization.
how Pol III transcription factors and Pol III complexes interact with chromatin to influence transcription of neighboring genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results demonstrate that the RNA polymerase III transcription complex can have profound effects on RNA polymerase II promoter activity, which may be relevant to the design of minimal yeast genomes.
the Pol III complex can have profound effects on transcription in the yeast nucleus, and that these effects may be relevant for human health and disease.
Pol II and Pol III transcription factors are involved in the regulation of gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pol III complex has a much more profound effect than previously appreciated on the expression of neighboring Pol II genes.
Pol III complexes exert local effects that are more global than appreciated, and that these effects are mediated by tDNA sequences.
the Pol III complex is an important factor in the regulation of Pol II transcription in yeast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pol III complex binding is not a simple `switch' that turns Pol II transcription on or off, but instead can exert more subtle effects on Pol II transcription that can be difficult to predict.
the presence of a tDNA or tRNA gene in an intergenic region can have a significant impact on the transcription of neighboring genes.

Pol II transcription is sensitive to the local environment of the Pol III transcription machinery, which may be important to consider when designing synthetic genomes or other synthetic biology constructs.
